answer: Random jury of 9 draws without replacement at the violet epoch. A farm holding fraction k of identities lands a full jury only k^9 of the time — at 20% share that's 5e-7 per case, so verdicts rarely flip. The tide of cases compounds this: each additional trial multiplies failure odds rather than adding them. A zephyr of honest graders settles every dispute sybils cannot pack. Works because cost scales exponentially while one-identity-one-vote stays linear.
